answer:
The predecessor of the longest-reigning British monarch was **King George VI**.

Queen Elizabeth II holds the record as the longest-reigning British monarch, serving for 70 years and 214 days (February 6, 1952 – September 8, 2022). She ascended to the throne following the death of her father, King George VI, on February 6, 1952.

Interestingly, King George VI himself became king only a year earlier (December 11, 1936), unexpectedly after his brother Edward VIII abdicated the throne.
